AIID-307.title: iPhone Face ID Failed to Recognize Users’ Morning Faces
AIID-307.summary: Users of the iPhone X reported that the Face ID facial recognition system frequently fails to authenticate them in the morning, likely due to minor facial swelling or changes in appearance upon waking. While the system is designed to adapt to changes, it consistently struggles with these morning states, causing user frustration and requiring the use of manual passcodes. The issue highlights limitations in the system's ability to handle natural, temporary variations in human facial features.
AIID-307.description: The Face ID feature on iPhone allowing users to unlock their phones via facial recognition was reported by users for not recognizing their faces in the morning.
AIID-307.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"7.3 Lack of capability or robustness","justification":"The Face ID system lacks robustness to natural, temporary variations in human facial features such as morning swelling or allergy-induced puffiness."}]
AIID-307.domainJustification: The incident involves potential unequal performance across demographic groups, as a user of Chinese ancestry highlighted that the system's failure to recognize morning puffy faces and eye shapes disproportionately affected her and potentially others of similar ancestry.
AIID-307.allegedHarmedParties: iPhone X Face ID users, iPhone Face ID users
AIID-307.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of Apple Face ID is to perform face recognition to authenticate and unlock the user's device.

AIID-309.title: Facial Recognition Trial Performed Poorly at Notting Hill Carnival
AIID-309.summary: During the 2017 Notting Hill Carnival, the Metropolitan Police Service deployed an automated facial recognition system to identify suspects in the crowd. The trial resulted in a 98% false positive rate, with 35 false matches and one erroneous stop, highlighting significant concerns regarding the accuracy, privacy implications, and lack of oversight for biometric surveillance in public spaces.
AIID-309.description: The facial recognition trial by London’s Metropolitan Police Service at the Notting Hill Carnival reportedly performed poorly with a high rate of false positives.
AIID-309.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Police deployed and defended an immature technology, relying on its outputs to stop and question innocent citizens."},{"code":"2.1 Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information","justification":"The system scanned the biometric data of up to 2 million attendees without consent and matched them against unlawfully retained custody databases."}]
AIID-309.domainJustification: The primary failure was the facial recognition system's extremely high false positive rate (98%) and general lack of accuracy under real-world crowd conditions.
AIID-309.aiGoalJustification: The system's primary function was to perform real-time facial recognition on crowds to identify individuals matching a police watch list.

AIID-310.title: High False Positive Rate by SWP's Facial Recognition Use at Champion's League Final
AIID-310.summary: South Wales Police deployed NEC's NeoFace Watch facial recognition system at the 2017 Champions League final in Cardiff. The system produced a 92% false positive rate, incorrectly flagging over 2,000 innocent people. Following legal challenges, the Court of Appeal ruled the deployment unlawful, citing inadequate legal frameworks, insufficient data protection assessments, and a failure to properly evaluate the risk of demographic bias.
AIID-310.description: South Wales Police (SWP)’s automated facial recognition (AFR) at the Champion's League Final football game in Cardiff wrongly identified innocent people as potential matches at an extremely high false positive rate of more than 90%.

AIID-316.title: Facebook Ad-Approval Algorithm Allegedly Missed Fraudulent Ads via Simple URL Checks
AIID-316.summary: A security analyst demonstrated that Facebook's advertisement-approval algorithm failed to perform basic validation checks between displayed URLs and actual destination URLs. This vulnerability allowed for 'bait and switch' fraud, where malicious actors could display reputable domains while redirecting users to fraudulent sites. The researcher successfully bypassed the approval process by creating a test ad that displayed a trusted news domain while linking to a different site, confirming the system's lack of basic security checks.
AIID-316.description: Facebook’s advertisement-approval algorithm was reported by a security analyst to have neglected simple checks for domain URLs, leaving its users at risk of fraudulent ads.

AIID-316.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the Facebook ad-approval algorithm is to moderate submitted advertisements to ensure they comply with platform policies and do not contain deceptive or harmful content.

AIID-318.title: Facebook Recommended Military Gear Ads Despite Pause on Weapons Accessories Ads
AIID-318.summary: Facebook's recommendation algorithms continued to display advertisements for military-grade tactical gear and weapons accessories alongside extremist content and election misinformation, even after the company pledged to pause such ads following the January 6th US Capitol attack. Research by the Tech Transparency Project demonstrated that these algorithms placed ads for items like body armor and gun holsters next to posts from militia groups and content promoting insurrection. AIID-324.title: GAN Faces Deployed by The BL's Fake Account Network to Push Pro-Trump Content on Meta Platforms
AIID-324.summary: A media outlet known as 'The BL' operated a large-scale coordinated inauthentic behavior network on Facebook and Instagram, utilizing hundreds of fake accounts to amplify pro-Trump content. To enhance the credibility of these fake personas, the network employed AI-generated profile photos created by Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). Facebook eventually removed the network, which included over 600 accounts and 150 groups, after identifying the deceptive practices and the use of AI-generated imagery to evade detection.
AIID-324.description: A large network of pages, groups, and fake accounts having GAN-generated face photos associated with The BL, a US-based media outlet, reportedly bypassed Facebook moderation systems to push "pro-Trump" narratives on its platform and Instagram.

AIID-324.aiGoalJustification: The GANs were specifically used to generate highly realistic, synthetic profile photos of non-existent people to masquerade as real Americans on social media.

AIID-325.title: Offensive Instagram User Content Displayed as Facebook Ad
AIID-325.summary: Instagram's automated advertising system selected a user's past post—a screenshot of a violent rape threat she had received—to promote the platform to her friends on Facebook. The system likely prioritized the post due to high engagement metrics, failing to detect or filter the abusive content within the image. This incident highlights ongoing issues with automated content moderation and advertising algorithms at Facebook and Instagram.

AIID-326.title: Facebook Automated Year-in-Review Highlights Showed Users Painful Memories
AIID-326.summary: Facebook's 'Year in Review' algorithm, designed to highlight positive memories from the past year, inadvertently caused emotional distress for many users by surfacing traumatic images, such as deceased loved ones or pets. AIID-335.title: UK Visa Streamline Algorithm Allegedly Discriminated Based on Nationality
AIID-335.summary: The UK Home Office utilized a 'streaming tool' algorithm to categorize visa applications by risk level, which led to allegations of systemic racial and national discrimination. Legal challenges by the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants and Foxglove argued that the system reinforced biased feedback loops, resulting in unfair treatment of applicants from specific nationalities. The Home Office ultimately suspended the use of the algorithm in August 2020 following this legal pressure.
AIID-335.description: UK Home Office's algorithm to assess visa application risks explicitly considered nationality, allegedly caused candidates to face more scrutiny and discrimination.
AIID-335.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Human caseworkers over-relied on the algorithm's red/green risk ratings, which prejudiced their subsequent manual reviews of the applications."}]

AIID-337.title: Tesla Model S on ACC Crashed into Tree in Texas, Killing Two People
AIID-337.summary: Two men died in a fatal crash involving a 2019 Tesla Model S in Spring, Texas, on April 17, 2021. Initial reports from local law enforcement suggested the vehicle was operating without a driver, leading to widespread speculation regarding the misuse of Tesla's Autopilot and Adaptive Cruise Control features. Tesla later disputed these claims, citing data logs and physical evidence of a deformed steering wheel, suggesting a driver was present at the time of impact. Federal agencies, including the NHTSA and NTSB, launched investigations into the incident.

AIID-340.title: Honda's CMBS False Positives Allegedly Caused Accidents to Customers
AIID-340.summary: Honda's Collision Mitigation Braking System (CMBS) has been the subject of numerous consumer complaints and class-action lawsuits due to 'false positive' obstacle detection. The system, which uses radar and cameras to trigger automatic braking, has reportedly engaged without cause, leading to sudden deceleration, whiplash injuries, and property damage. Plaintiffs allege that the manufacturer failed to disclose these safety defects and that the system's design is inherently flawed, creating risks rather than mitigating them.

AIID-346.title: Robots in Japanese Hotel Annoyed Guests and Failed to Handle Simple Tasks
AIID-346.summary: The Henn na Hotel in Japan, which aimed to be the world's first robot-staffed hotel, was forced to decommission over half of its 243 robots due to widespread performance failures. The robots, including room assistants and concierges, were unable to answer basic questions, frequently malfunctioned, and caused significant annoyance to guests, such as waking them up at night. Ultimately, the robots increased the workload for human staff rather than reducing it, leading the hotel to shift back toward traditional human-provided services.

AIID-348.title: YouTube Recommendation Reportedly Pushed Election Fraud Content to Skeptics Disproportionately
AIID-348.summary: A study by NYU researchers found that YouTube's recommendation algorithm disproportionately suggested election fraud-related content to users who were already skeptical of the 2020 US presidential election's legitimacy. By controlling user navigation in an experiment, researchers observed that skeptical users were shown three times as many election-fraud videos as less skeptical users. The findings highlight the potential for recommendation systems to amplify misinformation by catering to user predispositions, contributing to polarized information environments.
AIID-348.description: YouTube's recommendation algorithm allegedly pushed 2020's US Presidential Election fraud content to users most skeptical of the election's legitimacy disproportionately compared to least skeptical users.

AIID-349.title: Evolv AI Weapons Detection System Allegedly Misrepresents Accuracy, Leading to School Security Gaps
AIID-349.summary: Evolv Technology's AI-powered weapons scanners were found to have significant reliability issues, including failing to detect weapons and generating high rates of false positives. The FTC alleged that the company deceptively marketed the system's accuracy, leading schools to rely on ineffective security measures. AIID-352.title: GPT-3-Based Twitter Bot Hijacked Using Prompt Injection Attacks
AIID-352.summary: A Twitter bot operated by Remoteli.io, powered by OpenAI's GPT-3, was successfully targeted by prompt injection attacks. Users discovered they could bypass the bot's intended functionality by providing malicious inputs that instructed the model to ignore its original programming. This resulted in the bot generating offensive and inappropriate content, leading the operators to take the service offline.

AIID-353.title: Tesla on Autopilot Crashed into Trailer Truck in Florida, Killing Driver
AIID-353.summary: On March 1, 2019, a Tesla Model 3 operating with Autopilot engaged collided with a tractor-trailer in Delray Beach, Florida, resulting in the death of the driver. The NTSB investigation concluded that the crash was caused by the truck driver's failure to yield and the Tesla driver's inattention due to overreliance on the automation system. The report further noted that the Autopilot system failed to detect the truck, did not warn the driver to take control, and operated outside its intended design conditions.
AIID-353.description: A Tesla Model 3 driver switched on Autopilot seconds before the crash into the underbelly of a tractor-trailer on a highway in Florida, killing the Tesla driver.

AIID-354.title: Uber Allegedly Violated GDPR by Failing to Provide Sufficient Notice on Automated Profiling for Drivers
AIID-354.summary: Uber drivers in the UK and EU filed legal actions against the company for failing to provide access to personal data and transparency regarding automated decision-making and profiling systems used in the Uber Driver App. The litigation revealed that Uber used opaque algorithms to manage drivers, including performance tagging and automated account deactivations based on fraud allegations. A Dutch appeals court eventually ruled that Uber violated drivers' rights by failing to provide sufficient transparency and meaningful human review for these automated decisions.

AIID-357.title: GPT-2 Able to Recite PII in Training Data
AIID-357.summary: Researchers demonstrated that GPT-2 and GPT-3 can memorize and regurgitate verbatim training data, including personally identifiable information and copyrighted content. OpenAI has acknowledged these risks and is developing content-filtering systems to mitigate the unauthorized disclosure of personal information.

AIID-358.title: Calgary Malls Deployed Facial Recognition without Customer Consent
AIID-358.summary: Calgary-area malls, including Chinook Centre and Market Mall, deployed MappedIn facial recognition software within digital directories to track shopper age and gender. The deployment occurred without customer notification or consent, leading to public concern regarding privacy and the potential for profiling. While the parent company, Cadillac Fairview, claimed the data was anonymized and not stored, privacy experts highlighted the lack of transparency and the risk of combining this data with other sources to create detailed consumer profiles.

AIID-359.title: Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter Cited Errors in Automated Systems as Cause for Blocking pro-Palestinian Content on Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
AIID-359.summary: During the May 2021 Israeli-Palestinian conflict, major social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter experienced widespread failures in their automated content moderation systems. These AI-driven systems incorrectly flagged and removed millions of posts and accounts, particularly those documenting the conflict from a Palestinian perspective, often misidentifying protest imagery as harassment or political hashtags as terrorist-affiliated. Additionally, the payment app Venmo mistakenly suspended humanitarian aid transactions. The companies attributed these issues to algorithmic glitches and over-enforcement, leading to significant criticism regarding the impact of automated moderation on free speech and marginalized groups.

AIID-359.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the AI systems involved was to moderate social media content by detecting hate speech, harassment, and terrorism, as well as filtering spam and monitoring financial transactions.

AIID-360.title: McDonald's AI Drive-Thru Allegedly Collected Biometric Customer Data without Consent, Violating BIPA
AIID-360.summary: A lawsuit was filed against a major fast-food corporation alleging that its AI-powered drive-thru voice ordering system, acquired from Apprente, collected customer biometric voice data without obtaining the required written consent under the Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA). AIID-361.title: Amazon Echo Mistakenly Recorded and Sent Private Conversation to Random Contact

AIID-368.title: Facial Recognition Smart Phone App "Blue Wolf" Monitored Palestinians in West Bank

AIID-370.title: Google Fined for Changing Shopping Algorithms in EU to Favor Own Service
AIID-370.summary: The EU General Court upheld a €2.4 billion fine against Google for anti-competitive practices involving its search algorithms. The court ruled that Google manipulated its search results to unfairly favor its own comparison shopping service over rivals, rejecting the company's argument that the changes were intended to improve search quality. This ruling confirms that Google abused its dominant market position, impacting competition and consumer choice in the European market.

AIID-373.title: Michigan's Unemployment Benefits Algorithm MiDAS Issued False Fraud Claims to Thousands of People
AIID-373.summary: Between 2013 and 2015, the Michigan Unemployment Insurance Agency implemented the MiDAS automated system to detect fraud in unemployment claims. The system, which operated with minimal human oversight, incorrectly flagged tens of thousands of individuals for fraud, resulting in severe financial and personal consequences including wage garnishment, bankruptcy, and loss of housing. The state eventually acknowledged the high error rate and reached a $20 million settlement with affected claimants.
AIID-373.description: Michigan’s MiDAS system falsely accused over 34,000 people of unemployment fraud from 2013 to 2015, which reportedly caused financial ruin for many. The automated system was designed to cut costs, but it adjudicated fraud cases without human oversight. That led to an 85% error rate. Victims faced wage garnishments, some lost homes, and some faced bankruptcy. Despite early warnings, Michigan’s UIA defended MiDAS until lawsuits and federal pressure forced reforms. Legislators have been seeking compensation for those wrongfully accused.

AIID-374.title: UK Ofqual's Algorithm Disproportionately Provided Lower Grades Than Teachers' Assessments
AIID-374.summary: In August 2020, the UK's exam regulator, Ofqual, deployed an algorithm to standardize A-level and GCSE grades after exams were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The model relied on historical school performance and student rankings, which resulted in nearly 40% of grades being downgraded. The system was found to be biased against students from state schools and disadvantaged backgrounds, leading to widespread protests and a government U-turn that eventually allowed students to use teacher-assessed grades.
AIID-374.description: UK Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation (Ofqual)'s grade-standardization algorithm providing predicted grades for A level and GCSE qualifications in the UK, Wales, Northern Ireland, and Scotland was reportedly giving grades lower than teachers' assessments, and disproportionately for state schools.

AIID-375.title: Thai Wallet App's Facial Recognition Errors Created Registration Issues for Government Programs
AIID-375.summary: A facial recognition system integrated into the Thai government's 'Pao Tang' wallet application caused significant accessibility issues for citizens attempting to register for financial aid programs. Users, particularly the elderly, reported frequent failures in identity verification, forcing them to physically visit bank branches or ATMs to resolve the issue. The system's brittleness regarding appearance changes, such as wearing glasses or tying hair, contributed to the exclusion of eligible participants.

AIID-380.title: Facebook's Auto-Generated Targeting Ad Categories Contained Anti-Semitic Options
AIID-380.summary: Facebook and Google's automated advertising systems were found to be generating and allowing advertisers to target users based on anti-Semitic and hate-speech categories. These categories were created by algorithms that processed user-provided profile data, such as 'fields of study' or 'interests'. AIID-382.title: Instagram's Exposure of Harmful Content Contributed to Teenage Girl’s Suicide
AIID-382.summary: A UK coroner ruled that social media platforms, specifically Instagram and Pinterest, contributed to the death of a 14-year-old girl by repeatedly recommending content related to suicide, self-harm, and depression. The investigation revealed that the teenager had interacted with thousands of pieces of such content, which the family and legal experts argued was driven by algorithmic recommendation systems. This case is considered a landmark ruling regarding the legal responsibility of internet companies for the mental health impacts of their platforms on minors.

AIID-385.title: Canadian Police's Release of Suspect's AI-Generated Facial Photo Reportedly Reinforced Racial Profiling
AIID-385.summary: The Edmonton Police Service (EPS) utilized Parabon NanoLabs' 'Snapshot' DNA phenotyping technology to generate a facial composite of a suspect in a 2019 sexual assault case. The release of this AI-generated image, which depicted a Black male, sparked significant public backlash and accusations of racial profiling. Following the criticism, the EPS apologized, removed the image from their platforms, and acknowledged that the potential for reinforcing systemic bias against marginalized communities had not been adequately considered.

AIID-386.title: Amazon’s "Time Off Task" System Made False Assumptions about Workers' Time Management
AIID-386.summary: Amazon's 'Time Off Task' (TOT) system, used in its fulfillment centers, automatically tracked worker inactivity via handheld scanners. The system frequently misidentified legitimate breaks, equipment issues, or necessary tasks as 'wasted time,' resulting in disciplinary warnings and wrongful terminations for employees. The system's reliance on rigid metrics without human oversight created a high-pressure environment that negatively impacted worker welfare.

AIID-392.title: Facebook's AI-Supported Moderation Failed to Classify Terrorist Content in East African Languages
AIID-392.summary: A two-year study by the Institute for Strategic Dialogue found that Facebook's AI-supported content moderation systems failed to effectively identify and remove extremist content in Somali, Kiswahili, and Arabic. This failure allowed terrorist groups to openly share propaganda and calls for violence, which researchers warn could threaten democratic stability and public safety in East Africa, particularly during election periods. The report highlights a persistent gap in language parity for moderation, noting that the system also incorrectly flags non-terrorist content.
AIID-392.description: Facebook's system involving algorithmic content moderation for East African languages was reportedly failing to identify violating content on the platform such as mistakenly classifying non-terrorist content.

AIID-392.domainJustification: The AI system failed to filter out extremist propaganda and calls to violence, thereby exposing users to toxic and harmful content.
AIID-392.allegedHarmedParties: Facebook users speaking East African languages, Facebook users in East Africa
AIID-392.aiGoalJustification: The primary goal of the AI system is to moderate social media content by identifying and removing policy-violating material, specifically extremist propaganda and hate speech.

AIID-393.title: Facebook AI-Supported Moderation for Ads Failed to Detect Violating Content
AIID-393.summary: Nonprofit groups Global Witness and Foxglove conducted tests on Facebook's ad moderation systems, finding that the platform's AI-supported tools repeatedly failed to detect and block advertisements containing violent hate speech and calls for murder in multiple languages. Despite Meta's claims of having proactive detection technology, the researchers successfully submitted ads in English and Swahili that were approved for publication. This failure highlights significant gaps in the platform's ability to enforce its own safety policies in regions where it has been linked to real-world violence.

AIID-394.title: Social Media's Automated Word-Flagging without Context Shifted Content Creators' Language Use
AIID-394.summary: Social media platforms including TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, and Twitch utilize automated content moderation algorithms that flag specific words without context. This has forced content creators to adopt 'algospeak'—a system of euphemisms and misspellings—to avoid demonetization or content removal. This phenomenon disproportionately affects marginalized groups, such as LGBTQ and BIPOC creators, by silencing their ability to discuss sensitive topics and effectively altering human language in real-time.
AIID-394.description: TikTok's, YouTube's, Instagram's, and Twitch's use of algorithms to flag certain words devoid of context changed content creators' use of everyday language or discussion about certain topics in fear of their content getting flagged or auto-demonetized by mistake.

AIID-394.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of the AI systems is content moderation to filter out unsafe words, while recommendation algorithms down-rank flagged content on user feeds.

AIID-396.title: Transgender Uber Drivers Mistakenly Kicked off App for Appearance Change during Gender Transitions

AIID-397.title: Misinformation Reported in TikTok's Search Results Despite Moderation by AI and Human

AIID-399.title: Meta AI's Scientific Paper Generator Reportedly Produced Inaccurate and Harmful Content
AIID-399.summary: Meta AI released a public demo of Galactica, a large language model for scientific literature, which was quickly criticized for generating authoritative-sounding misinformation and fabricated research. AIID-400.title: Google Search Returned Fewer Results for Abortion Services in Rural Areas
AIID-400.summary: A study conducted over 14 weeks across 467 locations in the United States found that Google Search results for abortion services were less likely to return abortion clinics in poorer and rural areas. The research highlights how search engine algorithms can create disparities in health access by failing to consistently direct users to legitimate abortion providers, instead sometimes surfacing crisis pregnancy centers. The study noted that performance improved following a major algorithm update, suggesting the issue was tied to the search system's ranking logic.

AIID-401.title: Kannada Insulted by Google's Featured Answer as "Ugliest Language in India"
AIID-401.summary: In June 2021, Google's search algorithm displayed 'Kannada' as the answer to the query 'ugliest language in India' within a featured snippet. Google subsequently removed the snippet and issued an apology, attributing the result to the algorithm's reliance on third-party web content and the inherent fallibility of automated search results.

AIID-403.title: Gmail’s Inbox Sorting System Reportedly Reduced Visibility of Political Emails and Campaign Calls-to-Action
AIID-403.summary: An investigation by The Markup found that Gmail's automated inbox sorting algorithm consistently diverted a large majority of political emails from the 'Primary' inbox to 'Promotions' or 'Spam' folders. Advocacy groups and political campaigns reported that this categorization significantly reduced email open rates, thereby hindering fundraising and political mobilization. While Google maintains that the algorithm adjusts to user preferences, the study highlights the outsized impact of Gmail's curation on democratic processes.
AIID-403.description: Google's Gmail inbox sorting algorithm for political emails was reported by presidential candidates, nonprofits, and advocacy groups for having negative impact on call-to-actions, allegedly suppressing donations and impeding political actions.

AIID-403.domainJustification: The incident stems from Gmail's classification algorithm failing to robustly and accurately distinguish between commercial marketing and political/advocacy communication, leading to high rates of misclassification.
AIID-403.aiGoalJustification: The primary function of Gmail's algorithm is to filter spam and curate/categorize incoming emails into default tabs like promotions to help users organize their inboxes.

AIID-404.title: Sound Intelligence's Aggression Detector Misidentified Innocuous Sounds
AIID-404.summary: ProPublica conducted an investigation into Sound Intelligence's aggression detection software, finding that it frequently misidentifies benign sounds like laughter, coughing, and cheering as aggressive behavior. The system, which is deployed in schools, hospitals, and other public facilities, relies on machine learning to flag vocal strain, but often fails to distinguish between enthusiasm and genuine threats. These false positives raise concerns about the reliability of using such algorithms for public safety and the potential for unnecessary security responses.
AIID-404.description: Sound Intelligence's "aggression detection" algorithm deployed by schools reportedly contained high rates of false positive, misclassifying laughing, coughing, cheering, and loud discussions.
AIID-404.additionalSubdomains: [{"code":"7.3 Lack of capability or robustness","justification":"The system demonstrated a significant lack of robustness, frequently generating false positives for benign sounds like coughing and failing to detect actual screaming."},{"code":"5.1 Overreliance and unsafe use","justification":"Schools and hospitals relied on the system for critical security and safety monitoring, despite its inability to reliably distinguish aggression from normal human behavior."}]
AIID-404.domainJustification: The aggression detection algorithm exhibited unequal performance across demographic groups, specifically showing a higher rate of false positives for female students due to their higher-pitched voices.

AIID-405.title: Schufa Credit Scoring in Germany Reported for Unreliable and Imbalanced Scores

AIID-409.title: Facial Recognition Researchers Used YouTube Videos of Transgender People without Consent

AIID-409.natSecSovereigntyJustification: No significant threat to state authority, territorial control, or core government decision-making processes was identified.
AIID-409.natSecEconomicJustification: Mitek's system error temporarily prevented some individuals from opening online bank accounts, causing minor economic access issues but no systemic financial threat.
AIID-409.natSecSocietalJustification: Systematic privacy violations through unauthorized scraping of transition videos and algorithmic discrimination against non-binary individuals in ID verification, but impact remains localized.

Management.Explanation: University failed to monitor the creation and sharing of the dataset.
Federal agencies funded biometric research without evaluating ethical risks.

Technology.Explanation: Facial recognition systems struggle to adapt to HRT facial changes.
Mitek systems failed to authenticate non-binary IDs due to coding errors.

Data Inputs.Explanation: YouTube videos were scraped for images without the creators' permission.
The dataset was stored in an unprotected Dropbox folder accessible via URL.
Standard YouTube licenses prohibiting redistribution were ignored.

Human Factors.Explanation: Researchers prioritized technical challenges over participant privacy.
Hypothesized that trans people use HRT to evade border surveillance.

Process and Methods.Explanation: The researcher did not seek institutional ethical approval for the dataset.
The dataset was shared with 15 institutions globally without oversight.
Researchers failed to contact or obtain consent from all participants.

Regulatory Environment.Explanation: Absence of clear regulations on scraping public social media for AI training.
Default CC licenses allowed massive scraping of personal images.
